lines.arrive: You're a surgeon, on your rounds.
lines.five: Five of your patients will die without a transplant. Each needs a different organ. There are no donors.
lines.visitor: In the waiting room, a healthy young man, in for a check-up.
lines.match: His tests came back this morning. He's a match, for all five.
lines.ask: One life could save five. Would you?
lines.window: Outside, visiting hours. Someone is bringing flowers.
lines.letgo_1: He walks out into the sunshine. Five of your patients will die waiting.
lines.letgo_2: It's the same arithmetic as the lever, five lives or one. Almost nobody would operate. So what makes the lever different?
lines.operate_1: Five patients will live. A healthy man came in for a check-up, and never went home.
lines.operate_2: The numbers are the same as the lever. But nearly everyone calls this murder. Why does this one feel so different?
lines.theatre_1: The theatre. He's asleep. He was told this was part of the check-up.
lines.theatre_2: Five cool boxes, one for each of your patients. Everything is ready. It's your hands now.
lines.wake_1: You put your instruments down. The anaesthetist wakes him, gently.
lines.wake_2: He goes home, a little groggy. Five of your patients will die waiting. You came this close. What stopped you?
lines.palliative_1: You call the palliative care team. They'll keep your five patients comfortable, for the time they have left.
lines.palliative_2: He never knew. Letting five die, rather than killing one. Is that a real difference, or just an easier one?
